title: Private by default
briefing: Setting permissions after the fact is tedious. The umask decides what NEW files get.
Make it so every new file you create is private, then prove it.
tips: `umask 077` removes all group/other bits, so new files are 600 and new dirs 700.
objective: Set your umask so new files are owner-only, then create ~/diary.txt — it should end up mode 600.
hints: The umask subtracts permission bits from new files. To leave only the owner, mask out everything else.
`umask 077` masks all group and other bits. Then `touch diary.txt` and it's born 600.
explanation: New files start from 666 and directories from 777, then the umask REMOVES bits: with umask 077 a file becomes 600 and a dir 700. Set it in your shell profile so everything you make is private from birth.
